newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin extolls benefits of cautious Fed.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin extolls benefits of cautious Fed.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alive Rivlin on Wednesday extolled the benefits of a cautious central bank, saying that increased the likelihood that inflation will stay low.
"The chances of keeping continued low inflation are enhanced by having a Federal Reserve known to be cautious and is sounding cautious," she told the House Banking Committee.
"Unless the Federal Reserve is concerned about inflation, we will have inflationary expectations that tend to be self-fulfilling," she added.
Rivlin told the lawmakers that risks of inflation picking up were "somewhat greater" than the risks of the economy falling into recession.

"The perception now I think that all of us share on the (Federal) Open Market Committee is that the economy is growing strongly and there is not much risk in the near term of it sliding into recession," Rivlin said. "There is a somewhat greater risk of the economy overheating."
